 Assurer une surveillance appropriée et effectuer un suivi serré des principaux indicateurs de performance et adapter les stratégies en conséquence.

Diplôme universitaire dans un domaine pertinent tel que l’administration, la finance, l’économie, les mathématiques, les statistiques ou toute autre discipline connexe.

 About us
 Claio is a Montréal-based AI platform built for dental and healthcare practices. More than 400 practices across North America use Claio to answer patient calls, fill their schedules, and cut time spent on clinical notes. Clinicians report saving an average of 8+ hours a week on documentation.
 Our solutions: 
 AI Front Desk: answers patient calls 24/7, including nights and weekends. It books and reschedules appointments directly in the practice management system and hands calls to staff when needed.
 AI Scribe: turns patient conversations into structured clinical notes in the practice’s own templates and sends them straight to the practice management system. It can transcribe dozens of languages and then create notes in English, French, and Spanish.
 Our ecosystem: Claio plugs into the tools practices already use, with integrations into 17+ practice management systems, including Dentrix, Open Dental, Eaglesoft, MacPractice, and Dentitek. Claio was developed within the Manos Software Group and is backed by Valsoft Corporation, a Canadian company that builds and acquires vertical market software. That backing gives our agents a stable, growing product and a broader healthcare software portfolio behind them.
 We’re building a network of independent agents to grow our presence in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador.
 The role
 You’ll represent our product line to dental practices, DSOs, and labs in your territory, alongside other complementary, non-competing lines you already carry. You run your own business and set your own schedule.
 We provide product training, samples, marketing materials, and lead support.
 What you’ll do
 Introduce and sell our products to general dentists, specialists, DSOs, and labs.
 Build on your existing relationships and open new accounts through office visits, demos, and lunch-and-learns.
 Represent us at study clubs, regional dental meetings, and trade shows.
 Share monthly activity and pipeline updates, and pass along market feedback.
 Not just dental: Claio also serves medical practices, so you’re free to reach out to clinics in every medical specialty, from family medicine to specialist practices.
 5+ years of dental sales experience, as an independent agent or with a manufacturer or distributor.
 An active network of dental offices in New Brunswick, Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador. The territory is exclusive to you among independent agents, though Claio’s in-house reps may also sell there.
 A current portfolio of complementary lines (please list them so we can confirm there’s no conflict).
 Strong product-demo and presentation skills, and comfort with technical or clinical conversations.
 Reliable transportation and willingness to travel within the territory.
 Commission: Competitive commission rate on new bookings, paid quarterly and uncapped.
 Optional extras: An ongoing percentage bonus on subscription renewals and reorders from the accounts you sign.
 Support: product training, demo samples, marketing materials, and leads from our website / trade shows / distributor partners.
 Expenses: Claio provides demo accounts, marketing materials, and product training, and covers booth fees for Maritime dental events we ask you to attend (e.g. the New Brunswick Dental Society Conference). Out-of-territory travel we request is covered. You cover your own in-territory travel, phone, and office costs.

About Jesta I.S. 
 For more than 50 years, Jesta I.S. has helped retailers, wholesalers, and brand manufacturers grow through innovative enterprise software.
 Our composable retail and supply chain solutions connect merchandising, inventory, omnichannel commerce, warehouse operations, and supply chain management, enhanced by AI-powered insights from FarsightIQ.

 Do you know the retail industry, have strong relationships with its leaders, and enjoy turning complex business challenges into technology opportunities?

 Reporting to the Global Sales Director, you will focus on developing new business, building strategic relationships with retail executives, and helping retailers and brands identify technology solutions that address their operational challenges.
 We're looking for a commercially driven professional who understands how retailers operate, how technology decisions are made, and how to navigate complex enterprise sales cycles.
 Whether you come from enterprise technology sales or have worked within a retail organization championing technology solutions, your industry knowledge, established relationships, and ability to develop new business will be central to your success.
 This opportunity is open to candidates residing in the United States.

 You'll contribute directly to Jesta's growth by:
 Expanding our market presence: Identify, develop, and secure new business opportunities with mid-market and enterprise retailers across North America.
 Building strategic relationships: Establish trusted partnerships with retail executives, decision-makers, and industry influencers.
 Driving revenue growth: Develop a strong pipeline, advance complex sales opportunities, and consistently work toward revenue targets.
 Delivering business value: Translate operational challenges into compelling technology solutions supported by consultative selling and ROI-driven business cases.
 Developing long-term partnerships: Identify opportunities to expand customer relationships and support sustainable account growth.
 What You'll Be Doing 
 Business Development & Sales Execution
 Own the full enterprise sales cycle, from prospecting and discovery through solution presentations, negotiations, and closing.
 Develop and execute strategic territory and account plans to generate qualified opportunities and achieve revenue targets.
 Build and maintain a healthy sales pipeline, ensuring accurate CRM records, forecasting, and opportunity management.
 Leverage your retail industry network, targeted prospecting, and strategic partnerships to uncover new business opportunities.
 Consultative Selling & Client Relationships
 Engage senior executives and decision-makers across merchandising, operations, supply chain, finance, and IT.
 Understand customers' operational priorities and position Jesta's ERP, retail, omnichannel, and supply chain solutions accordingly.
 Develop compelling value propositions, business cases, and proposals that demonstrate measurable business benefits.
 Lead complex sales discussions, coordinate demonstrations, respond to RFPs, and negotiate commercial agreements.
 Build lasting customer relationships while identifying opportunities for account expansion.
 Collaboration & Market Development
 Collaborate with Solution Consulting, Product, Marketing, Professional Services, and Customer Success throughout the sales process.
 Develop relationships with consultants, advisory firms, systems integrators, and technology partners to generate opportunities.
 Represent Jesta at industry events, conferences, and partner engagements.
 Use CRM platforms, sales analytics, and approved AI-assisted tools to improve prospecting, account research, and sales productivity.

 Essential Qualifications
 Enterprise Sales Experience: 3–5+ years of relevant experience in enterprise technology sales or a retail business role involving the evaluation, promotion, or commercialization of technology solutions.
 Proven Business Development Results: Demonstrated success generating new business, managing complex opportunities, and achieving commercial objectives.

 Experience using Salesforce, HubSpot, or comparable CRM platforms.
 Exposure to composable, API-enabled, or AI-powered enterprise software.
 Experience developing business through consultants, systems integrators, or technology partners.
 Bachelor's degree in Business, Marketing, Commerce, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

 Excellent communication, negotiation, and executive presentation skills.
 Strong relationship-building abilities and a collaborative approach to working with internal and external stakeholders.
 Ability to work independently, manage priorities, and maintain effective communication with colleagues and customers.
 Strong written and spoken English skills for communicating with North American customers and partners.
 Willingness to travel within North America for customer meetings, industry events, and business development activities.

 At Jesta, you'll represent established enterprise technology solutions, build meaningful relationships with retail industry leaders, and contribute directly to our growth across North America.

The endpoint is where we meet the adversary directly, and where the people we serve, the analysts and defenders protecting hospitals, banks, and government networks, need us most. Their mission is our mission, and this role carries that responsibility for the endpoint and XDR market. Like Elastic itself, the role is distributed by design.
 This business was born when Elastic acquired Endgame in 2019, a pioneer in endpoint prevention, detection, and response with roots in defending national security networks. We extended that protection philosophy to Linux and cloud-native environments with the Cmd acquisition in 2021. The result today is Elastic Defend, and its record in independent testing reflects the quality of the work: Elastic Security was the only vendor to score 100% protection in both the AV-Comparatives Real-World and Malware Protection Tests for all of 2025, and the only vendor among 16 to earn a perfect malware protection score in the 2026 Business Security Test, with zero false alarms on the software businesses actually run.  This role is open for a straightforward reason. Our product leader is retiring, and we are organizing product management around our two core businesses: SIEM and analytics, which will be led by a proven leader already at Elastic, and endpoint, where we are looking outside for someone who brings a fresh perspective from this market.  Shape where we invest and where we choose not to, building the case with data and customer evidence.
 Own how endpoint and XDR fit the broader Elastic Security platform story, so a customer who lands with endpoint expands into the platform and a SIEM customer sees why our endpoint belongs next to it.
 Put customers first. Visit them where they are, participate in deals and win/loss reviews, enable the field, and represent Elastic at tradeshows and industry events. This work requires regular travel.

 Clear executive communication with executive leadership, CISOs, sales leadership, and industry analysts.

 The Kitchen brings together a range of disciplines and capabilities. It’s a team of creatives, producers, data analysts and social experts working together to deliver remarkable ideas that live in a variety of mediums, from everything from social to TV. We want individuals who are passionate about producing award-winning work and have an innate drive to their craft and are eager to generate innovative ideas both within and outside of the brief. 
 THE ROLE 
 We’re looking for an experienced, well-rounded Senior Editor to join our Production team in Toronto and play an important role in our growing in-house post-production capability. 
 Reporting directly to the Executive Producer, Production , you’ll work closely with a robust team of Producers across Toronto and Chicago, as well as our Creative, Account and broader agency teams and, from time to time, directly with our brand partners. 
 Our work lives primarily within the food, beverage and food-adjacent space and spans everything from fast-turnaround social and digital content to broadcast commercials and larger integrated advertising campaigns. We’re looking for someone who understands the pace, craft and collaborative nature of agency production and is equally comfortable digging into an edit independently, working alongside a Creative team or leading a supervised session with internal and brand stakeholders. 
 WHAT YOU’LL DO 
 Lead offline editorial across broadcast, digital, social, branded content and integrated advertising campaigns. 
 Edit work across a wide range of formats and durations, from short-form and social content through :06, :15, :30 and longer-form storytelling. 
 Partner closely with Producers, Creatives, Account teams and brand stakeholders throughout the post-production process, from initial assemblies through creative approval and delivery. Participate in pre-production and creative conversations when appropriate, helping teams anticipate editorial opportunities, coverage needs, post-production considerations and potential efficiencies before cameras roll. 
 Participate in and lead supervised edit sessions, confidently navigating feedback and contributing editorial solutions in real time. 
 Bring a strong editorial perspective to the work, helping teams find the strongest story, performance, pacing, structure and creative execution rather than simply executing a brief. 
 Create and implement motion graphics as part of day-to-day editorial, including supers, typography, transitions, end cards, graphic treatments and other motion elements required to bring an edit to completion. 
 Perform light colour correction and grading when appropriate, while collaborating with specialized external partners for more advanced colour and finishing requirements. 
 Manage multiple edits, versions, aspect ratios, formats and deliverables across projects of varying scale and complexity. 
 Prepare and adapt work across broadcast, social and digital specifications, including short-form cutdowns and platform-specific versioning. 
 Perform stock music searches and provide a creative POV to creatives/CDs on music direction 
 Collaborate with external post-production partners across advanced motion design, animation, VFX, colour, audio and finishing when projects require additional specialization. 
 Maintain highly organized project files, media, working assets and archives throughout the lifecycle of a project. 
 Perform editorial QC and prepare final files for review, approval and delivery, ensuring accuracy across picture, audio, graphics, supers, aspect ratios, versioning and technical specifications. 
 Work confidently within established post workflows while helping us continue to develop and strengthen our growing in-house editorial capability. 
 Work on-site from our Liberty Village office during designated in-office days, currently Tuesday and Thursday. 
 Work effectively across both in-person and remote editorial workflows, collaborating with teams and stakeholders across Toronto and Chicago. 
 Experience with collaborative review platforms such as Frame.io and remote post-production workflows. 
 Share knowledge, best practices and technical expertise with the broader team, contributing to the continued development of our editorial standards and capabilities. 
 Have experience with Extreme Reach submission or uploading for broadcast deliverables. 
 WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR 
 7+ years of professional editorial experience within an advertising agency, in-house agency, production company or post-production environment, with agency and/or in-house experience strongly preferred. 
 A strong portfolio or reel demonstrating editorial craft, creative thinking and a high level of polish across finished work. 
 Demonstrated experience working on food, beverage and/or food-adjacent advertising and content . 
 Extensive experience with professional NLE systems and contemporary post-production workflows. 
 Advanced proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and comfort working within the broader Adobe Creative Suite . 
 Strong proficiency in After Effects , with the ability to independently design, build and implement motion graphics required for everyday advertising and content work. 
 Working knowledge of Photoshop and an understanding of how design assets move between creative and editorial workflows. 
 Experience with DaVinci Resolve or Baselight is an asset. 
 Comfort performing light colour correction and grading, with an understanding of when work should transition to a dedicated colourist or finishing partner. 
 Experience with advanced 2D or 3D animation is a significant plus, but not a requirement. 
 Strong understanding of media management, codecs, formats, versioning, conforming and preparing projects for downstream colour, VFX, audio and online finishing. 
 Experience working directly with Creative, Production and Account teams as well as clients or brand stakeholders. 
 Strong creative instincts and an ability to interpret feedback, contribute ideas and recommend editorial solutions. 
 Comfortable working independently while managing competing priorities, tight timelines and multiple stakeholders. 
 Highly organized, detail-oriented, collaborative and calm within a fast-moving production environment. 
 Demonstrated ability to take editorial ownership of a project from initial assembly through approval, proactively identifying creative and technical needs rather than waiting for direction at each stage. 
 WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE 
 You become a trusted creative and production partner across the agency, someone Producers, Creatives and brand teams want in the room early and rely on when the work gets complicated.

Product philosophy

More importantly, we’ve helped over 20,000 restaurant owners, and saved them nearly $200 million in fees.

Role Overview

Owner's promise to a restaurant isn't software, it's revenue. When a guest lands on a restaurant's site, we want them to find what they're craving, trust what they see, and check out without friction, whether or not the owner ever touches a setting.

As we scale, we're expanding our product engineering leadership to ship faster, raise the bar on the guest ordering experience, and build the systems that make it work across thousands of restaurants. As the Engineering Manager for OLO, you'll lead a team of full-stack engineers building the guest web ordering experience, from menu, cart and checkout to promotions, photos, and the menu quality systems that make about 10,000 merchant-written menus convert like they were designed by a pro. Next, we're taking OLO to enterprise and multi-location brands, and pushing guest conversion toward 10% through disciplined experimentation. This role is equal parts product intuition and technical execution. You'll be trusted to make hard prioritization calls, ship experiments that move revenue, and grow a team that embodies engineering excellence.

We move with urgency, bias toward simplicity, and expect our leaders to be hands-on when needed. If you're energized by ownership, measurable impact, and solving real problems for small business owners, we'd love to hear from you.

Why we’re looking for you

Owner's promise to a restaurant isn't software — it's revenue. OLO is where that promise gets converted: the guest web ordering experience (menu, cart, checkout, promotions) plus the automated systems that find and fix menu quality problems across roughly 10,000 menus written by merchants we don't control.

We treat conversion as an automated system, not a design review. We build rubrics, detection, and remediation, then prove every change with an experiment. Next, we're taking OLO upmarket to enterprise and multi-location brands and pushing conversion toward 10%.

We're looking for a Senior Engineering Manager to lead the team through that, keep it healthy, and hold a high bar on what we ship and what we cut.

This role is 100% remote and can be based anywhere in the United States or Canada.

Our Stack

 - Web / Growth: React, Next.js, TypeScript — guest web ordering, menu quality, experimentation platform

 - Backend & Services: Node.js, MongoDB → PostgreSQL (migration in flight), Temporal, Datadog

 - Language: TypeScript everywhere

The Impact You'll Have

 - Build the experimentation engine that pushes guest conversion toward 10%, across checkout, fulfillment, merchandising, and promotions

 - Take OLO to enterprise and multi-location brands, with the reliability and menu complexity they need

 - Get >90% of menus, including POS-integrated ones, to our menu quality bar, and build the system that keeps live menus optimized as they change

 - Scale photo coverage using guest sourcing, auto-replating, licensed catalogs, and generated combo images, each tied to measured GPV lift

 - Rebuild promotions from the ground up: redemption UX, badges, auto-apply, and merchandising

 - Cut fulfillment selection errors and finish the Postgres migration

What we’re looking for

 - 3+ years of engineering management, leading teams of 6–10+ engineers on customer-facing product

 - Track record of running growth or conversion programs: metrics, A/B testing at scale, funnel analysis

 - Experience scaling a product for enterprise or multi-location customers

 - Strong prioritization: you can take a roadmap bigger than your team and make hard, clear calls

 - Technical credibility in full-stack web (React/TypeScript, Node.js) and data-heavy systems

 - Cares about team health and has led people through heavy or repetitive workloads

 - Excellent cross-functional partner to PM, design, and adjacent teams

Compensation and benefits

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced, hands-on Senior Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) to join the Release Integration Testing (RIT) function within Release & Feature Qualification for AI Inference Core.

The Production Engine for Inference Core — turning integrated features into reliable production releases.

In this role, you will develop sophisticated test automation, validate complex AI inference systems, investigate cross-stack failures, and drive improvements in release quality and reliability. You will work across AI frameworks, runtime, compiler, kernels, distributed systems, infrastructure, and hardware to identify integration risks and ensure production readiness.

This is a highly technical, hands-on engineering role requiring strong software development, automation, and debugging skills. You will independently own complex testing initiatives, contribute to test architecture and release qualification strategies, and collaborate closely with engineering teams to improve system reliability.

Release Integration Testing (RIT) is the bridge between feature qualification and release qualification. Feature teams retain ownership of feature design, feature-level qualification, and feature regression. RIT focuses on integration readiness, cross-stack validation, regression stability, and first-pass rollout triage for AI Inference Core.

What Makes This Role Distinct

 - Software engineering applied to quality: Design and develop scalable test automation, frameworks, diagnostics, and tooling to validate complex AI inference systems—not just execute test cases.

 - Cross-stack technical challenges: Debug and validate interactions across AI frameworks, runtime, compiler, kernels, distributed systems, infrastructure, and hardware.

 - Integration and release ownership: Independently drive integration testing, regression validation, and release qualification activities for complex inference-core features.

 - Inference-path validation: Identify and test high-risk interactions across runtime, host, device programming, memory, scheduling, and model execution.

 - Production reliability: Improve master and release-branch stability through robust automation, failure analysis, and actionable quality metrics.

 - Technical collaboration: Partner with SDETs, software engineers, infrastructure teams, and release owners to resolve complex issues and improve engineering efficiency.

What You Will Do

 - Design, develop, and maintain automated test frameworks, tools, and infrastructure to validate AI inference software across multiple components and system layers.

 - Independently own integration testing and qualification activities for complex inference-core features, identifying dependencies, interaction risks, and potential coverage gaps.

 - Develop and execute comprehensive end-to-end, integration, regression, and system-level tests across AI frameworks, runtime, compiler, kernels, infrastructure, and hardware.

 - Analyze unit, simulation, benchmark, feature-test, and integration results to assess readiness, identify gaps, and provide evidence-based recommendations for release qualification.

 - Investigate and debug complex cross-stack failures, perform root cause analysis, collaborate with engineering teams on fixes, and implement automated tests to prevent regressions.

 - Improve master and release-branch stability by identifying regressions, triaging failures, validating fixes, and contributing to release-quality metrics and reporting.

 - Build and enhance internal tooling for test automation, diagnostics, monitoring, dashboards, CI/CD workflows, and release qualification pipelines.

 - Collaborate with feature engineering, Integration, Core Infrastructure, and release teams to improve test coverage, accelerate debugging, and support coordinated feature rollouts.

 - Contribute to test architecture, risk-based testing strategies, and continuous improvements in automation efficiency, system observability, and release reliability.

 - Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers through code reviews, debugging sessions, and sharing testing best practices.

Minimum Skills & Qualifications

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals with professional experience developing software, automated testing frameworks, or test infrastructure.

 - Proficiency in Python, Go, or a similar programming language, with demonstrated experience writing maintainable, production-quality code.

 - Experience designing, developing, and maintaining automated tests and frameworks for complex software systems.

 - Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including the ability to investigate failures across multiple components, analyze logs and system behavior, and identify root causes.

 - Solid understanding of software testing methodologies, including integration testing, system testing, regression testing, and end-to-end validation.

 - Experience working with CI/CD pipelines, test automation infrastructure, and software development workflows.

 - Working knowledge of operating systems, networking, distributed systems, or systems-level software concepts.

 - Ability to independently own complex technical problems, prioritize testing efforts, and drive issues through resolution.

 - Strong communication and collaboration skills, with experience working across multiple engineering teams to deliver reliable software.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience testing or developing distributed systems, infrastructure software, runtime systems, compilers, kernels, or other low-level software.

 - Experience with AI/ML infrastructure, LLM inference, model deployment, multimodal workloads, or large-scale compute environments.

 - Exposure to hardware accelerators, GPU systems, software/hardware integration, or high-performance computing.

 - Experience building scalable test frameworks, distributed test systems, release pipelines, or internal developer tools.

 - Familiarity with performance testing, profiling, observability, fault injection, reliability engineering, or production failure analysis.

 - Experience with containers, Kubernetes, cloud infrastructure, cluster orchestration, or large-scale distributed computing environments.

 - Experience using debugging and observability tools to diagnose complex system-level issues.

 - Experience working in fast-paced engineering environments, including startups or teams developing complex systems software.

What Success Looks Like

 - You independently deliver robust, scalable automation and test infrastructure that improves integration and release qualification.

 - Complex cross-stack defects are identified and resolved earlier in the development cycle, reducing issues discovered during final release qualification or production.

 - Regression testing provides reliable, actionable signals that improve master and release-branch stability.

 - Debugging cycles are shorter through improved diagnostics, automation, and effective collaboration across engineering teams.

 - Test coverage and qualification processes evolve to support increasingly complex AI inference features and workloads.

 - Your technical contributions improve release predictability, engineering efficiency, and overall system reliability.

 - You are a trusted technical contributor who helps raise engineering quality through strong code, sound judgment, and mentorship.

Location

ABOUT BASETEN

Baseten powers mission-critical inference for the world's most dynamic AI companies, like Cursor, Notion, OpenEvidence, Abridge, Clay, Gamma, and Writer. By uniting applied AI research, flexible infrastructure, and seamless developer tooling, we enable companies operating at the frontier of AI to bring cutting-edge models into production. We're growing quickly and recently raised our $1.5B Series F https://www.baseten.co/blog/announcing-our-series-f/, led by Altimeter Capital, Conviction Partners, and Spark Capital. Join us and help build the platform engineers turn to ship AI products.

THE ROLE

Baseten is seeking talented and experienced Software Engineers to join our Platform team within the Infrastructure organization. As a member of Baseten's Platform Team, you will own the systems that let every engineer at Baseten prove their code works before it reaches production. Our product runs mission-critical AI inference for customers who measure downtime in dollars per second, which means our internal bar for correctness, performance, and failure tolerance has to be exceptional.

Your focus is the full testing stack: fast and reliable unit test tooling, integration harnesses that spin up realistic environments on demand, load and performance testing for GPU-backed inference workloads, and resilience testing that deliberately breaks things so our customers never have to find out what happens when a node dies mid-request. This is a builder role with org-wide leverage. You won't be writing tests for other teams — you'll be building the frameworks, harnesses, and feedback loops that make writing good tests the path of least resistance, and you'll set the standards for what "well-tested" means at Baseten.

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Own Baseten's testing strategy end to end — define the standards, the tiers, and the tooling that engineering teams build against.

 - Build and maintain unit, integration, load and performance testing frameworks

 - Design end to end test infrastructure that provisions realistic dependencies on demand — ephemeral Kubernetes namespaces, containerized service dependencies, etc.

 - Build resilience and chaos testing capabilities: fault injection, network partition and latency simulation, pod and node failure scenarios, dependency degradation, and automated verification that our systems degrade gracefully and recover.

 - Attack test suite reliability head-on — flake detection and quarantine, test impact analysis and selective execution, parallelization, and aggressive reduction of end-to-end CI wall time.

 - Build observability into the testing layer itself: coverage reporting, test health dashboards, failure triage tooling, and clear signals about which areas of the codebase are under-tested.

 - Create project templates and shared libraries so new services start with a complete testing setup on day one.

 - Partner directly with product and infrastructure teams — embed where needed, understand their hardest testing problems, and turn one-off solutions into platform capabilities.

 - Mentor engineers across the org on testing practice and raise the collective bar through code review, documentation, and internal advocacy.
   
   

REQUIREMENTS

 - Strong proficiency in Go and/or Python, with hands-on experience building test tooling and libraries used by other engineers.

 - Deep experience with testing frameworks and their internals — pytest, Go's testing package, testify, testcontainers, or equivalents — including the ability to extend them, not just use them.

 - Experience designing integration test infrastructure for distributed systems, including ephemeral environment provisioning and dependency management.

 - Practical experience with load and performance testing tools (k6, Locust, Vegeta, JMeter, Gatling, or similar) and the judgment to interpret results and drive action from them.

 - Solid Kubernetes and Docker fundamentals — you can build test infrastructure that runs on and tests against real cluster environments.

 - Advanced understanding of CI/CD, including how to keep large test suites fast, deterministic, and trustworthy at scale.

 - A track record of measurably improving testing culture on an engineering team — you have opinions on what to test, what not to test, and where the ROI actually is.

 - Are excited about building foundational infrastructure and are comfortable working independently on ambiguous, high-impact technical challenges

BENEFITS

 - Competitive compensation, including meaningful equity

 - Paid parental leave

 - Fertility and family-building stipend through Carrot

 - (U.S. only) Company-facilitated 401(k)

Internal Program Manager, Artificial Intelligence 
 The Internal Program Manager, Artificial Intelligence coordinates the adoption and day-to-day operations of AI platforms and tools used internally (e.g., Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and M365 Copilot). The role measures adoption and makes the value created visible; supports teams with initiatives and the implementation of approved practices; tracks requests; serves as the single point of entry for internal AI requests; and manages the platform usage model, including groups, distribution, usage limits, and budgets. The incumbent connects teams, ambassadors, and decision-making bodies to promote the effective and responsible use of AI.
 Responsibilities 
 Measurement, initiative tracking and reporting:
 Develop and maintain indicators that provide insight into adoption, outcomes, and opportunities for improvement, beyond consumption volumes.
 Produce reports and aggregated views by business area for leadership, and provide managers with tools to monitor and support their teams.
 Maintain existing directories and drive the development of the internal AI practices and use-case directory; track significant initiatives and their contribution within each business area based on established thresholds.
 Highlight commonalities and opportunities for sharing across business areas.
 Maintain the inventory of internal AI platforms, tools, and use cases (business area, business owner, and risk level assigned by AI governance), in collaboration with IT and AI Governance.
 Report to AI Leadership and AI Governance on the application of approved practices, observed gaps, and usage trends.
 Adoption and Enablement:
 Build and maintain regular relationships with the various areas of the organization to understand AI uses, needs, and pain points.
 Ensure operational coordination of the AI Ambassadors Committee, follow up on its initiatives, and facilitate the flow of information.
 Recommend practices and implementation guides; support teams in improving how they use AI.
 Foster a regular cadence of internal AI communications, coordinate communications with ambassadors who contribute to the content, and maintain targeted monitoring of AI tools and practices.
 Escalate situations involving risk or requiring arbitration to the appropriate stakeholders.
 Communicate new policies, standards, and approved practices through AI ambassadors and managers, and ensure they are understood.
 Gather feedback from users and ambassadors on policies, practices, and learning resources, and bring it forward to AI Governance and Learning Leadership.
 Identify AI literacy needs by role, for both effective and responsible use, and communicate them to Learning Leadership.
 Communication and Presentations
 Explain AI concepts, issues, and developments in clear, accessible language for users across all business areas through guides, FAQs, learning capsules, and demonstrations.
 Design and produce presentations, documents, and other communication materials for users, managers, and leadership.
 Present adoption status, results, and recommendations to executives and committees, adapting the message and level of detail to the audience.
 Facilitate information sessions, demonstrations, and practice-sharing sessions for teams and AI ambassadors.
 New request-management process:
 Implement and operate the new AI request-management process.
 Serve as the single point of entry for all internal AI requests; route them to the appropriate bodies, including the AI Lab when experimentation is required; and track their progress.
 Maintain request documentation and decision logs, and follow up with requestors after decisions are made.
 Apply established intake criteria, including business owner, intended use, and data involved, to ensure requests are complete before they are routed.
 Route requests in accordance with established escalation paths and decision rights, based on the level of risk and type of request.
 Platform usage model:
 Define and maintain the distribution model, groups, usage limits, and usage budgets for approved internal AI platforms, and monitor their use.
 Make authorized routine adjustments and recommend changes that require a decision or specialized intervention.
 Collaborate with IT, Security, AI Governance, and AI Leadership on groups, feature access, usage limits, and usage budgets.
 Identify usage anomalies, including unusual volumes or unexpected access or group assignments, and report them to IT and Security.
 Notify the appropriate bodies of significant vendor changes to platforms, including models, features, or terms, that may require review.
 Contribute to the periodic review and potential retirement of platforms and features by providing usage and adoption data.
 Incidents and Operational Compliance
 Receive and document reports of incidents or risk situations related to AI use; route them to the appropriate stakeholders—Security, AI Governance, Legal, or Human Resources, as applicable—and follow each case through to closure.
 Monitor compliance with usage policies and approved practices, and report gaps to AI Governance.
 Document lessons learned from incidents and gaps, and incorporate them into implementation guides.
Education 
 Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline, such as information technology, business administration, communications, data science, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
 Experience 
 Approximately 6 to 10 years of relevant experience in technology adoption, digital-tool operations, cross-functional coordination, or a related field.
 Hands-on experience with generative AI platforms and tools in a professional environment, such as Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, and M365 Copilot.
 Experience defining and monitoring indicators and producing reports for leadership and managers.
 Experience presenting and communicating to senior executives and leadership committees.
 Skills and Competencies 
 Comfort working within the AI ecosystem, including a functional understanding of platforms, their impacts, risks, and the changes they introduce, particularly with respect to data, access, and connectors.
 Data and metrics analysis skills, with the ability to interpret usage data with nuance and connect observations to intended outcomes.
 Ability to coordinate requests and initiatives involving multiple stakeholders without formal authority.
 Ability to support users and teams in improving how they use AI.
 Ability to collaborate effectively with IT, Security, Learning, Governance, Program Management, and leaders across business areas.
 Technical curiosity, sound judgment, strong organizational skills, and clear communication.
 Ability to explain complex technical concepts in clear, accessible terms for varied audiences.
 Proficiency with presentation and document-production tools, such as PowerPoint and Word, and the ability to create professional-quality presentations and documents.
 Comfort presenting to executives and committees with a concise, decision-oriented message.
 This position requires bilingualism, as the incumbent will work with documentation in both French and English and communicate orally and in writing with French- and English-speaking partners, clients, vendors, and colleagues.
 Assets: 
 Experience with data visualization and dashboard development.
 Experience with the functional administration of SaaS or AI tools.
 Experience facilitating or coordinating a community of practice.
 Knowledge of AI use cases across multiple business functions.

ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

ABOUT PRODUCTION ENGINEERING

Production Engineering is Ramp's infrastructure ownership layer. We exist to make Ramp faster, more reliable, and more scalable — and we do that by being embedded in the problems, not adjacent to them.

A few things that define how we operate:

 - One team, one company, one objective. There is no "infra team" and "product team" — there is Ramp. We share the company's goals as our own. When a product team struggles with reliability or scalability, that is our struggle.

 - If reliability or scalability is at risk, we own it. We don't wait to be invited, and we don't ask whose code it is. If a system is slow, if it breaks, if it won't scale — that's ours to lead, regardless of where it lives in the stack.

 - We go first, and we go fast. When the path isn't obvious, we don't wait for someone else to find it. We move with urgency, propose the solution, align the stakeholders, and stay in until it's done — not until our ticket is closed.

 - We lead the way. We find the next problem before it finds us. And when we solve it, we don't just fix it for ourselves — the patterns and standards we establish become the foundation the rest of Ramp builds on. That's not a side effect of the job; it's the job.

 - We stay calibrated. Speed means nothing if we're moving in the wrong direction. We regularly stop and ask honestly whether what we're working on is still the highest-leverage thing we could be doing — the discipline that makes sure our effort compounds toward what actually matters.

You cannot build the future of finance on shaky infrastructure.

OUR TEAMS

Production Engineering is organized into teams — but we think about teams differently. Teams are mutable. We build them around what needs to be done, not around what we need to do given the teams we already have. The structure below reflects our current priorities; it will evolve as Ramp does.

Right now, we operate across four areas:

 - Compute — the foundation everything runs on: container orchestration, networking, load balancing, edge infrastructure, and the deployment systems that get code from engineers' laptops to production reliably and at scale

 - Storage — databases, caching, object storage, and the data infrastructure that underpins everything

 - Workflows & Messaging — the systems that power Ramp's financial workflows and event-driven architecture

 - Internal Infrastructure — the platform that makes every builder at Ramp faster and more autonomous: observability, cost attribution, and CI/CD systems that give teams visibility into what they build and what it costs

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Production Engineers at Ramp are full software engineers who happen to specialize in infrastructure. You write production code, you own systems end-to-end, and you drive technical outcomes across the organization — not just within your team.

Day to day, you will:

 - Build and operate critical infrastructure across Ramp's compute, storage, messaging, and observability stack — owning the systems that handle real financial transactions at scale.

 - Drive architectural change — not just flag problems. When you surface a reliability or scalability issue, you own the path forward: you propose the solution, find the owners across engineering, and stay in until it's resolved.

 - Partner with product teams at the design phase — reviewing architectures, embedding golden paths, and making it easy to build correctly the first time.

 - Build Ramp's next level of scale — you'll be a hands-on contributor to the most consequential infrastructure shift happening right now: our move to a cellular architecture, enabling Ramp to scale, reach international markets, operate in highly regulated and constrained environments (e.g. FedRAMP), and deliver on enterprise-grade SLAs.

 - Enable AI-native engineering — as Ramp builds increasingly AI-powered products, PE is the team that makes sure the platform can support them. You'll proactively partner with product teams on AI infrastructure patterns, define the golden paths that turn one-off solutions into reusable foundations, and stay ahead of emerging challenges before they become blockers.

 - Build developer tooling and self-service infrastructure — so that other teams can answer their own questions (cost, performance, reliability) without involving PE.

 - Participate in on-call rotation — and more importantly, use every incident as a signal to eliminate the root cause, not just resolve the symptom.

 - Lead across the company — PE doesn't just review designs or show up when called. We proactively initiate cross-team architectural reviews, and we take full ownership of company-wide reliability and scalability initiatives: identifying the problem, proposing the solution, aligning the stakeholders, and staying in until it's done.

WHAT WE LOOK FOR

We don't hire for a checklist. We hire for the instincts that make someone exceptional on this team.

The mindset we're looking for:

 - You can't walk past something broken without wanting to fix it — and you don't stop at the workaround. You find the root cause and eliminate the class of problem.

 - You think in systems, not tasks. You understand that "fixing the bug" is step one; making it so the bug can't happen again is the job.

 - You move with urgency but without chaos. You know when to go fast and when to slow down and do it right.

 - You treat product teams as your users. You build for them, communicate with them proactively, and measure success by how much faster they can ship. But you're also an owner — when something is broken or blocking, you don't wait to be asked. We win when our customers win.

 - You leave things better than you found them. Every system you touch, every process you encounter — you move it forward. Not always dramatically, but always directionally. You picked it up in a certain state; you leave it in a better one.

 - You are equally comfortable reading a database query plan, reviewing a system design doc, writing a Terraform module, and jumping into an incident at 2am.

Experience profile:

 - 2+ years of software engineering experience shipping high-quality architectures for critical systems 

 - Strong software engineering fundamentals — you write clean, well-tested, production-ready code

 - Hands-on experience with distributed systems at production scale

 - Experience with at least one major cloud provider (AWS preferred)

 - Familiarity with observability practices (SLOs, error budgets, alerting, dashboards)

 - Track record of leading technical projects end-to-end, including cross-team coordination

 - Comfortable using AI tooling and coding agents as part of your everyday engineering workflow — we expect our engineers to leverage these tools to move faster and think bigger

Bonus (not required):

 - Experience with cellular or multi-tenant architecture patterns

 - Prior work on workflow orchestration systems (Temporal)

Who we are: 
 Accenture Song Service helps leading brands turn customer interactions into an engine for growth, moving service beyond a cost center to something that builds trust, loyalty, and share of wallet. Our Service practice works end to end: we shape the vision and strategy for the service function and help clients implement and run it, innovate the products and services customers rely on, equip client customer service and customer experience teams with the right technology and talent, and turn customer data into insights that strengthen client’s relationship with their customers.
 Service AI & Data puts AI at the heart of this work. We help clients reinvent how they serve their customers and support their people: conversational AI and AI agents that resolve customer needs across voice, chat, and messaging; copilots that help service agents and field teams do their best work; and the data foundations, data lakes, reporting, and analytics agents that turn every interaction into insight. The strategies we shape and the experiences we design are delivered into production at enterprise scale.
 Who you are: 
 You are an AI Value Engineer who bridges the gap between business need and AI build in customer service. You identify where AI can create real value in a client's service operation, quantify it in terms leaders care about, and track the value AI initiatives create long after launch, so clients can see exactly what their investment is returning. You are equally at home building a value model, facilitating a stakeholder workshop, and shaping a rapid prototype.
 You bring a commercial, outcome-driven mindset to everything you do. You ask sharp questions, challenge assumptions with data, and explain tradeoffs in plain language to client leaders and engineers alike. You thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, moving between engagements and picking up new domains quickly. Above all, you are a curious, collaborative teammate who makes the people around you better.
 The work: 
 Embed with client service and business teams to understand how their service operation creates and loses value, from contact volumes and drivers to agent workflows, operating costs, and customer outcomes.
 Identify and quantify AI value hypotheses, analyzing contact drivers, interaction data, and operational metrics to find where AI can improve containment, handle time, first-contact resolution, CSAT, retention, and cost-to-serve.
 Run use-case discovery and prioritization workshops with client stakeholders, mapping use cases against value, feasibility, and risk to build a prioritized AI roadmap.
 Build business cases and ROI models that client leaders can trust and defend, including baselines, benefit assumptions, build and run costs, and sensitivity analysis.
 Run cost-benefit and scenario analyses to identify the best solution, comparing options such as build versus buy, platform and model choices, levels of automation, and phased rollouts, and making the tradeoffs behind each one clear.
 Build the full cost of AI into the business case, including run costs such as token usage, inference, and platform fees, how those costs scale with volume, and the human oversight AI solutions still need, such as review and escalations, so clients can see the true cost per interaction of each option.
 Map value to specific build initiatives, translating each prioritized use case into scope, success metrics, and requirements that Forward Deployed Engineers and AI Solution Engineering teams can build against.
 Define service scorecards with client leaders, selecting and prioritizing the KPIs that matter most for their business goals, such as lowering cost-to-serve, improving customer experience, or retaining revenue, and balancing efficiency metrics like containment and handle time against quality metrics like resolution, CSAT, and customer effort, so AI is never optimized for one at the expense of the other.
 Define how value will be measured before a build begins, setting baselines, KPIs, and measurement plans, and using control groups or A/B tests to attribute impact to the AI solution rather than other factors.
 Track the value AI initiatives create over time, creating and maintaining value dashboards and benefits tracking across a client's portfolio of AI use cases. Pull data from client data warehouses and data lakes using SQL or Python to validate savings and results against the business case.
 Run regular value reviews with client business, finance, and service leaders, reporting realized versus planned value, flagging early when an initiative is off track, and recommending what to fix, scale, or stop.
 Feed realized value back into the roadmap, so the next round of AI investment is prioritized by proven results rather than projections.
 Tell the story with data, designing clear visualizations, dashboards, and executive-ready presentations that turn complex analysis into a simple narrative: where value is, what it is worth, and what to do next, so clients can make confident investment decisions.
 Contribute reusable value models, benchmarks, and use-case libraries from the field so our teams can size and prove value faster on the next engagement.
 Help onboard and mentor junior teammates, and contribute to project debriefs and team POVs.
 Here's what you'll need: 
 3+ years of professional experience in management or technology consulting, business analysis, value engineering, product management, or customer service operations and analytics.
 3+ years of experience working on customer service, contact center, or customer experience projects or operations, with a strong command of service metrics such as containment, first-contact resolution, average handle time, CSAT, and cost-to-serve, and their financial impact. Experience should include: Experience building business cases, ROI models, and value measurement frameworks for technology or AI initiatives, and tracking realized value after launch.
 Experience defining service scorecards or KPI frameworks and prioritizing metrics based on business needs.
 Strong analytical and financial modeling skills in Excel or Google Sheets, including cost-benefit and scenario analysis.
 Hands-on SQL skills to pull and analyze data from data warehouses and data lakes (Python is a plus), and experience with a BI tool such as Power BI, Tableau, or Looker.
 Strong data visualization and storytelling skills, with the ability to choose the right visual for the message and build a clear, compelling narrative from data for executive audiences.
 A working understanding of AI and LLM capabilities, limits, and cost drivers, such as token usage, model choice, and inference volume, enough to assess feasibility, compare AI and human cost per interaction, and challenge assumptions about what AI can deliver.
 Familiarity with enterprise AI platforms on Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud.
 Willingness to travel regularly to client locations.
 Bonus points if you have: 
 Experience with contact center analytics, such as contact driver and intent analysis, speech and interaction analytics, or workforce management data.
 Experience designing experiments, such as A/B tests and control groups, to measure business impact.
 Experience with benefits realization or value tracking practices, including working with client finance teams to validate savings and returns.
 Experience with customer service platforms.
 A portfolio of business cases, value models, or prototypes you can walk us through.
 Bachelor's degree in business, economics, engineering, computer science, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

Float is Canada’s intelligent financial operating system, combining modern financial services and software to help businesses spend, save, and grow. AI USE IN OUR HIRING PROCESS

ABOUT THE ROLE

Float is investing in the next chapter of its Customer Success Operations function. As our Revenue Operations Manager, Customer Success, you'll play a foundational role in shaping how Customer Success scales by building the systems, programs, and operating rhythms that help our customers grow and our team operate more effectively. While we already leverage Salesforce across the business, this role will lead the evolution of our dedicated Customer Success tooling and operating model as we continue to scale.

We're looking for a Revenue Operations Manager, Customer Success to build the systems, processes, and insights that enable our Customer Success team to scale efficiently while driving customer retention, expansion, and operational excellence. You'll partner closely with Customer Success leadership, RevOps, Finance, Product, and Sales to transform strategic ideas into repeatable operating programs that improve customer outcomes and business performance.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Design and optimize the end-to-end post-sales (Customer Success) customer journey across onboarding, adoption, renewal, and expansion.

 - Build and own the Customer Success operating system, creating scalable processes that improve retention, expansion, forecasting, and operational efficiency.

 - Evaluate, implement, and optimize the Customer Success technology stack, driving adoption and enablement across the team.

 - Develop and continuously improve customer health scoring frameworks, risk indicators, and expansion signals.

 - Build and own recurring forecasting programs and target setting for customer retention and expansion, ensuring leadership has accurate visibility into business performance.

 - Create scalable account planning and risk management programs for Float's largest customers.

 - Partner with Customer Success leadership to define CSM workflows, operating rhythms, success metrics, and performance measurement.

 - Translate complex and fragmented customer data into clear recommendations and actionable insights for Customer Success and GTM leadership.

 - Partner cross-functionally with RevOps, Product, Finance, Sales, and Data teams to improve systems, reporting, customer handoffs, and operational efficiency.

 - Identify opportunities to automate manual work and streamline workflows so Customer Success Managers can spend more time driving customer value.

 - Establish reporting, dashboards, and operating cadences that help leadership make faster, data-informed decisions.

ABOUT YOU

 - You Put Customers First. You're constantly thinking about how operational improvements ultimately create a better customer experience.

 - You Act Like an Owner. You proactively identify opportunities, solve problems, and take accountability for outcomes.

 - You Think Big and Move Fast. You're energized by building from zero to one and thrive in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

 - You Constantly Learn and Grow. You actively seek feedback, adapt quickly, and continuously improve your craft.

 - You Raise the Bar. You balance speed with quality and are always looking for ways to improve how teams operate.

 - You Win as a Team. You build strong relationships across functions and know that great operations require great collaboration.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 5+ years of experience in Customer Success Operations, Revenue Operations, or a similar strategic operations role with end-to-end ownership.

 - Experience working in a consumption or usage-based SaaS business where forecasting, customer growth, and compensation models are more complex is highly preferred.

 - Proven experience building scalable Customer Success programs, processes, and operating rhythms from the ground up.

 - Hands-on experience selecting, implementing, and optimizing Customer Success technology and operational tooling.

 - Strong analytical skills with the ability to turn complex, fragmented data into clear business recommendations.

 - Experience building customer health models, forecasting frameworks, and executive reporting.

 - Exceptional cross-functional communication skills with experience partnering closely with Customer Success, Sales, Finance, Product, and RevOps leaders.

 - A bias toward action—you identify problems, propose solutions, and drive execution without waiting for direction.

OUR HIRING PHILOSOPHY

 - Collaborate with an ambitious and supportive team

Le Groupe du financement structuré et du financement de projets d’EDC, l’une des plus grandes équipes de financement de projets internationaux au Canada, joue un rôle important dans le financement de fusions et acquisitions, de projets et d’infrastructures à l’échelle mondiale.  About the Team 
The AI Model Serving team is the engine behind every production Workday agent and machine learning use case. We own the services that power all production AI workloads, acting as both the gateway to vendor-hosted LLMs (GCP, AWS Bedrock, Gemini) and the primary platform where Workday hosts and scales its internal models.
We operate at scale, hosting thousands of traditional ML models across sharded Ray Serve clusters and maintaining Workday's production model registry. Our platform consistently handles ~2,000 requests per second, peaking at over 10,000 RPS in our largest clusters.
In the year ahead, our engineering roadmap is highly ambitious. We are focused on:
Scaling Architecture: Upgrading our systems to seamlessly support 20+ new AI agents going into production.
Hosting Open-Weight LLMs: Designing the infrastructure to host and tune open-source LLMs directly within our stack.
Performance & Reliability: Architecting optimizations to drive down core latency while maintaining the rock-solid stability our high-throughput production systems demand.
Enterprise Governance: Hardening our unified vendor interface and implementing advanced cost-governance controls.
Our culture is built on focus, camaraderie, and high performance. We are a friendly, dedicated group that takes pride in building and operating one of the most heavily used services at Workday. You will play a central role in making critical design decisions, driving outcomes across the team, and setting a positive and inclusive team culture. 
 Your work will directly impact Workday's ability to serve AI at scale — from traditional ML models to the latest large language models powering Workday's agents.

Private markets are one of the largest, most complex, and most underserved corners of global finance. Our mission at Juniper Square is to unlock their full potential. Juniper Square’s Customer Success organization is responsible for ensuring customer health and satisfaction, driving product usage and adoption, and delivering strong commercial outcomes for both our clients and the business. You’ll act as a strategic advisor, ensuring customers realize the full value of Juniper Square as they grow.

 - Manage a portfolio of 220+ client accounts, leading them through the customer journey following onboarding

 - Build strong, trust-based relationships while leveraging digital and scaled engagement to drive product adoption and customer satisfaction

 - Identify and drive opportunities for retention and expansion within your book of accounts

 - Proactively monitor customer health and usage trends to identify risks and opportunities for growth

 - Support and own renewal conversations and mid-contract escalations, while collaborating cross-functionally to identify and drive expansion opportunities

 - Develop advanced knowledge of the customer, product, and industry

QUALIFICATIONS

 - Demonstrated experience learning advanced knowledge on technical subject matters and curiosity to grow in knowledge

 - Consistent, thoughtful use of AI across your core CSM deliverables, including the instinct to set it up with good context and a real example of where it improved quality, speed, or customer readiness.

COMPENSATION
